newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury says to propose simplifying tax code.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury says to propose simplifying tax code.

text.p: The Treasury Department will soon issue a proposal aimed at simplifying the tax code, Kenneth Krepsky, deputy assistant Treasury secretary for tax policy, said Wednesday.
He told a tax conference the plan would be released in the spring but would not give any details of what it would contain.

"The package is intended to ... provide we hope substantial simplification to ease compliance for taxpayers and to ease the administrative burden on the IRS (Internal Revenue Service) in applying the law, while at the same time maintaining revenues," he said.
"This package is within the context of the president's overriding agenda ... which is a balanced budget by 2002," he said.
Clinton's budget included a "placeholder" for this plan, meaning there were no specific proposals outlined but "the budget commits the administration to putting this package forward," Krepsky said.
Asked whether the plan would contain certain proposals, he replied, "everything is on the table."
